Sets pretrial and trial procedures for handling classified information in federal criminal cases, so that a defendant cannot force the government to choose between dropping the case and disclosing secrets.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 94 Stat. 2025](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/94/2025){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 4: the court may allow deletions, summaries, or substitutions in classified discovery.
- Sec. 5: the defendant must give notice of intent to disclose classified information.
- Sec. 6: hearings on use, relevance, and admissibility, with substitutions or stipulations in place of the classified original.
- Sec. 7: the government may take an interlocutory appeal.

## Why it matters

It is procedural and creates no new secrecy privilege, but it is what makes prosecutions under the [Espionage Act](espionage-1917.qmd) and terrorism cases workable in ordinary courts.

## Current status

In force.
